findings.evidence: `<input id="password-input" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" minlength="8" required="">`
findings.fix: Add visible helper text under the password field (e.g. "At least 8 characters") similar to the helper text used under the phone field.
findings.violation: The 8-character minimum is enforced only via the `minlength` attribute; there is no visible text telling the user the password requirement before they submit and get a validation error.

findings.fix: Differentiate the tokens, e.g. use `autocomplete="tel"` for the primary and remove/alter autocomplete (or use `"tel-national"`/no autocomplete) for the secondary field.
findings.violation: Both the primary phone (`phone-input`) and secondary phone (`phone2-input`) use the identical `autocomplete="tel"` token, so browser autofill cannot distinguish them and may fill both fields with the same number.

findings.fix: Make the field optional (remove `required`) and change to `type="url" autocomplete="url"`, or remove the field entirely if it doesn't belong on a consumer signup form.
findings.violation: A "Company website" field is marked required on a consumer account-creation form, which will block signups from users who have no company website; it also uses `type="text"` with no `autocomplete="url"` instead of the appropriate URL input type.

findings.evidence: `placeholder="Must be 8 digits"` with no `maxlength` or `pattern` attribute
findings.fix: Add `maxlength="8"` and `pattern="[0-9]{8}"` so the constraint is enforced, and keep persistent helper text rather than relying solely on the placeholder.
findings.violation: The "must be 8 digits" requirement is communicated only via placeholder text (which disappears on focus) and is not actually enforced by any validation attribute.

findings.fix: Either remove this field from the signup form or add explanatory text about why it's needed and how it will be protected, and reconsider whether it belongs here at all.
findings.violation: The form collects a sensitive "Account number" with no explanation of what it's for and no autocomplete/privacy handling, which is an unusual and risky data request during basic account creation.

findings.fix: Increase `size` to at least 10, or remove the `size` attribute and control width via CSS.
findings.violation: The postal code input is sized to show only 3 characters, which is too narrow for valid postal codes (e.g. 5-digit US ZIP codes or longer international formats), causing the entered text to scroll out of view.
The select element has no `name` attribute, so the chosen shipping speed will never be included in the submitted form data.

findings.fix: Remove one of the duplicate options or clarify how they differ (e.g. delivery time cutoffs).
findings.violation: "Overnight" and "Next-day" are redundant/synonymous shipping-speed options, which will confuse users about what distinguishes them.

findings.fix: Remove the redundant field, or if a legally distinct name is genuinely needed, relabel it clearly (e.g. "Legal name, if different from above") and explain the difference.
findings.violation: This field duplicates the "Full name" field already collected in `row-name`, with the same `autocomplete="name"` token, forcing users to enter their name twice with no clear distinction between the two.

findings.fix: Make the field optional, and move the font-size styling into a shared stylesheet so all inputs render consistently.
findings.violation: "Organization name" is required on what otherwise appears to be a personal consumer signup form, which will block individual customers from completing registration; the inline `font-size:13px` style also makes this field visually inconsistent with the rest of the form.

findings.fix: Remove the ad hoc inline float/width styling and lay out the label/input pair consistently with the rest of the form (e.g. via a shared CSS class).
findings.violation: The label is floated and width-constrained but the adjacent input has no matching layout styling, which will cause the label and input to misalign or overlap.

findings.fix: Replace with a constrained input such as a `<select>` of time ranges, or add a placeholder/pattern specifying the expected format.
findings.violation: "Preferred contact time" is a required free-text field with no format guidance (e.g. "9am - 5pm"), so submitted values will be inconsistent and hard to use.

findings.fix: Remove the button if unused, or move it out of the field sequence (e.g. into a header/info section) and give it a clear, documented purpose.
findings.violation: This button sits between the contact-time field and the date-of-birth fieldset with no apparent purpose or associated handler, interrupting the form's field flow and tab order.

findings.evidence: `<select id="dob-day-select" autocomplete="bday-day" required="">` (and the month/year selects have the same pattern)
findings.violation: None of the three date-of-birth `<select>` elements have a `name` attribute, so the selected day, month, and year will never be submitted with the form.

findings.fix: Expand the year range to cover realistic customer ages, and add a disabled/blank default option (e.g. "Year") so the field isn't silently pre-filled with a valid-looking value.
findings.violation: The year options only span 1950 - 2009, excluding anyone born before 1950 (older than 76 in 2026) or after 2009 (younger than 17), and since there's no blank default option, a `required` select pre-selects the first option (1950) so a user could submit an unintended birth year without actively choosing one.
